intent: The area of the page whose right click or long press opens its ContextMenu at the pointer.
typical_uses: A wrapper around the content the menu's actions apply to, such as a table row, a list entry or a canvas

dont_use_when.situation: A visible button that opens a menu when clicked

invariants.text: A right click (the `contextmenu` event) opens the menu at the pointer, and a single-finger touch held for 500 ms that moves no more than 10 px opens it at the touch point; the browser's own context menu is suppressed over the trigger while the root is enabled.
The trigger renders a plain `<div>` with no role and no tabindex, and the primitive attaches no key handler to it; the menu opens only through the `contextmenu` event or a touch long press.
context-menu.module.css sets `user-select: none` on the trigger, so text inside it cannot be selected by dragging.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through context-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A file entry that opens the menu on right click
A table row rendered as the trigger

bad.title: A made-up asChild prop to reuse the child element
bad.why: The trigger has no `asChild`; it falls through to the forwarded `<div>`, which still wraps the row. Pass the element through `render` instead.
